Subject: Urgent: private cluster throughput cliff and 503 spike (WardenBridge Prod-VPC)

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp drop in token throughput and a spike in 5xx errors on our Redwood private deployment in us-west-2 (prod namespace) starting ~07:55 PDT. Key numbers:
- Aggregate tokens/sec down ~40% vs baseline (rolling 1h)
- p95 latency up from ~220ms to ~720ms for our long-sequence model routes
- 5xx rate increased from 0.2% to 4.1% (mostly 503/502)

This coincided with your 04:00 AM maintenance—specifically the runtime kernel update (llm-runtime v4.1.2) that was pushed to our cluster. We've attached the SRE logs and a small KPI snapshot.

We can provide full request traces when you need them. This is customer-impacting for several workflows (clinical triage and real-time notes ingestion). Please advise immediate mitigation steps — throttling is not an option for us given SLAs.

Anoop
Senior Platform SRE
WardenBridge Health

Thanks for the fast heads-up, Anoop — sorry for the disruption. We're on it.

Immediate plan (first 30–60m):
- Roll back llm-runtime kernel update on a small canary subset to validate regression (we need your OK to flip canary nodes).
- Temporarily increase autoscaler target by 30% (to buy headroom) and disable aggressive batching on the affected routes.
- If rollback isn't possible quickly, we have a hot-patch that disables the fused-int8 matmul path (likely culprit). Vivek will lead the patch.

Vivek, can you confirm quick triage (root cause hypothesis: quantized kernel mismatch causing heavy CPU fallbacks and blocking on IO)? Laura / Marissa — keeping you looped for account communications and exec visibility; this will need an exec sync once we have mitigation validated.

Quick tech read and suggested remediation:

What I see (first-pass):
- The new llm-runtime v4.1.2 introduced an optimized fused int8 matmul kernel that assumes a specific alignment for KV cache strides. For the WardenBridge model config (long sequences + per-request varying prefix caching) that alignment isn't always met.
- When misaligned, the kernel falls back to a CPU path that serializes token generation and triggers thread contention and long tails on the worker process. That matches the p95/p99 and 5xx symptoms.

Immediate fixes (order):
1) Hot patch: restore previous kernel selection logic for the fused-int8 path (attached kernel-diff.patch). This is a safe change and can be applied to a single node group.
2) Canary: roll canary group back to v4.1.1 kernel selector to validate positive delta.
3) Short-term config: set runtime flag --kv-cache-stride-safe=true and disable inter-request batching for the impacted model route.
4) Post-mitigation: run a targeted load-profile (attached KPI snapshot) and sweep quantization tests across sample inputs.

Risk: minimal for patch, medium for a full rollback (depends on operator window). Patch will avoid a full rollback while we stabilize.

I've attached kernel-diff.patch and a pointer to the internal runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/wardenbridge/incident-20280601

Vivek Kulkarni
